findings.title: Unconditional UTF-8 decode raises UnicodeDecodeError for non-UTF-8 or cap-truncated bodies
findings.evidence: Body bytes are joined and decoded with no charset negotiation and no error handling, ignoring the charset in Content-Type and any multi-byte sequence cut off at the cap: `return b"".join(chunks).decode("utf-8")`. A server returning ISO-8859-1/GBK text, or a body whose final multi-byte char straddles the max_bytes boundary, makes the call raise instead of returning text.
findings.recommendation: Capture the declared encoding inside the with block (e.g. encoding = response.encoding or utf-8) and decode the joined bytes after the block with an explicit errors policy (e.g. errors=replace or errors=strict documented in the docstring); alternatively expose an encoding parameter so the null/unknown-charset case is caller-controlled.

findings.title: Cap bounds bytes but not wall-clock time; slow-drip response can stall the caller forever
findings.evidence: The timeout is passed straight to requests, which applies it per socket operation (connect and each read), not to the total transfer: `    with requests.get(url, timeout=timeout, stream=True) as response:`. A server that sends one byte just under the read timeout keeps the streamed loop alive far beyond 10 seconds (1 MB at 1 byte / 9 s is weeks), so the size cap provides no latency bound. Reachable with any slow or adversarial origin; note this depends on server behaviour, hence minor.

findings.recommendation: Record a deadline (time.monotonic() + timeout) before the loop and raise on each iteration when it is exceeded, or wrap the loop in a total-budget check, so the cap bounds both bytes and elapsed time.

findings.title: except ValueError also encloses the ResponseTooLarge raise, silently swallowing cap failures if the class changes
findings.evidence: The try block is broader than the single int() conversion it needs to guard, and it also contains the size-cap raise: `            except ValueError:`. Today ResponseTooLarge derives from Exception so it propagates, but any refactor that makes ResponseTooLarge a ValueError subclass (or an int() raising a different exception type) turns an enforced cap into a silent pass-through, defeating the whole guard. The pass also hides malformed headers with no trace, making such servers hard to diagnose.

findings.recommendation: Narrow the try to only the conversion (parse declared into an int inside try/except, then compare and raise outside it), so the cap failure path can never be caught by the parse-error handler.

findings.title: No tests cover the size-cap paths despite the security-relevant guard
findings.evidence: The diff adds only the module; no test exercises the boundary condition or the two distinct enforcement paths: `            if total > max_bytes:`. Untested branches include: declared Content-Length over the cap (should raise before streaming), declared header absent or unparsable (must fall through), body exactly at max_bytes (must succeed), and body one byte over (must raise and not accumulate the offending chunk).
